title: The Single Jordan Block: Nilpotent Shift and Minimal Polynomial (Sub-OQ-01)
description: Sub-OQ-01 of the Jordan-Normal-Form infrastructure problem minpoly-charpoly-oq-01, discharging the load-bearing spectral API of a single Jordan block. Mathlib v4.26.0 has no `jordanBlock` matrix and no theorem for the minimal polynomial of a Jordan block, so all results are built from scratch. The centerpiece is the closed form for powers of the nilpotent shift `N = jordanBlock R 0 d` — `(N^k) i j = 1` iff `j = i + k` — from which follow `N^d = 0`, the sharp lower bound `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` (nilpotency index exactly `d`), and the main result `minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d` over a field: the Jordan block is non-derogatory, its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial. Self-contained (restates `jordanBlock` rather than importing the parent); build-verified sorry-free and axiom-free (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound).

originalContributions: shift_pow_apply: the closed-form power law for the strict upper-shift `N = jordanBlock R 0 d`, `(N^k) i j = 1` iff `(j:ℕ) = (i:ℕ) + k` else `0`, proved by induction on `k` over a general commutative ring — the single fact behind both nilpotency and its sharpness.
shift_pow_dim_eq_zero: `N^d = 0` (the shift is nilpotent of index at most `d`), read off directly from the power law since `j < d ≤ i + d`.
shift_pow_pred_ne_zero: `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` for `d ≥ 1` over a nontrivial ring — the `(0, d-1)` entry is `1` — establishing that the nilpotency index is exactly `d`.
isNilpotent_shift: `IsNilpotent (jordanBlock R 0 d)` packaged from the `N^d = 0` witness.
jordanBlock_sub_smul_one: the single-block Jordan–Chevalley split `jordanBlock R λ d - λ • 1 = jordanBlock R 0 d` (i.e. `A - λI` is the pure nilpotent shift).
minpoly_jordanBlock: over a field, `minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d` for `d ≥ 1` — the Jordan block is non-derogatory (minimal polynomial equals characteristic polynomial).

mathlibDependencies.description: The minimal polynomial divides any polynomial that annihilates the element. Used to get `minpoly K A ∣ (X - C λ)^d` from `(A - λI)^d = 0`.
For a prime `p`, `a ∣ p^n ↔ ∃ i ≤ n, Associated a (p^i)`. With `X - C λ` prime this pins the minimal polynomial to `(X - C λ)^m` for some `m ≤ d`.
`X - C a` is prime in `K[X]` over a field. Supplies the primality hypothesis for `dvd_prime_pow`.
Two monic associated polynomials are equal. Upgrades the `Associated (minpoly) ((X-C λ)^m)` from `dvd_prime_pow` to an equality (both are monic).
`aeval A (minpoly K A) = 0`. Used to transport the sharp lower bound: the minimal polynomial annihilates `A`, so `N^m = 0`, which combined with `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` forces `m = d`.
`algebraMap K (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) K) λ = λ • 1`. Rewrites `aeval A (C λ)` into the scalar matrix, exposing `aeval A (X - C λ) = A - λ • 1`.
Every element of a finite-dimensional algebra over a field is integral; gives `IsIntegral K A` for a matrix, hence `minpoly K A` is monic.

overview.historicalContext: The single Jordan block is the atom of Jordan Normal Form: over an algebraically closed field every matrix is similar to a block-diagonal sum of Jordan blocks, and the entire theory reduces to understanding one block. A single block `J = λI + N` splits into a scalar (semisimple) part `λI` and the strict upper-shift `N`, which is nilpotent — this is the Jordan–Chevalley decomposition specialised to one block. That `N` is nilpotent of index exactly equal to the block size, and consequently that the block is non-derogatory (its minimal and characteristic polynomials coincide, both `(X-λ)^d`), are classical facts appearing in every treatment of canonical forms (Axler §8; Dummit & Foote §12.3; Hoffman & Kunze §7). Mathlib v4.26.0 has extensive minpoly/charpoly infrastructure but no `jordanBlock` matrix at all, so this API — the JNF gap flagged in the parent problem's roadmap — is built here from scratch.
overview.problemStatement: **Sub-open question (minpoly-charpoly-oq-01-oq-01)**: Define the Jordan block `jordanBlock R λ d` and establish its basic spectral API — the power law for the nilpotent shift `N = jordanBlock R 0 d`, that `N^d = 0` while `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`, and that over a field `minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d`. These are the load-bearing facts consumed by the downstream nilpotent-canonical-form (OQ-01-OQ-02) and global-assembly (OQ-01-OQ-04) sub-questions.
overview.text: **Resolution (complete)**: A single closed-form power law `(N^k) i j = [j = i + k]` (proved by induction on `k`) does all the work. The `d`-th power pushes the diagonal band of `1`s off the matrix, giving `N^d = 0`; the `(d-1)`-th power leaves a single `1` in the top-right corner, giving `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`. The minimal polynomial then follows by a UFD argument: `(A - λI)^d = 0` gives the upper bound `minpoly ∣ (X-C λ)^d`, primality of `X - C λ` pins `minpoly = (X-C λ)^m`, and the sharpness `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` forces `m = d`. The whole entry is build-verified sorry-free and axiom-free.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Power law (`shift_pow_apply`)**: induction on `k`. The base case is `N^0 = 1`, whose `(i,j)` entry is `[i = j] = [(j:ℕ) = (i:ℕ) + 0]`. The step uses `pow_succ` (`N^(k+1) = N^k · N`) and `Matrix.mul_apply`; right-multiplication by `N` picks out the single surviving index `l = j - 1` (always a valid `Fin d` element when `j ≥ 1`), and `Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem` collapses the sum. This deliberately multiplies on the *right* so the surviving index is `j - 1` (never overflows) rather than `i + 1` (may overflow the block).

**`N^d = 0` and `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`**: both are immediate corollaries of the power law — the first because `j < d ≤ i + d`, the second because the `(0, d-1)` entry is `1` (needs `R` nontrivial for `1 ≠ 0`).

**Minimal polynomial (`minpoly_jordanBlock`)**:
1. `aeval A ((X - C λ)^d) = (A - λ•1)^d`; and `A - λ•1 = N` (`jordanBlock_sub_smul_one`), so this is `N^d = 0`. Hence `minpoly K A ∣ (X - C λ)^d` via `minpoly.dvd`.
2. `X - C λ` is prime, so `dvd_prime_pow` gives `Associated (minpoly K A) ((X - C λ)^m)` with `m ≤ d`; both monic, so `minpoly K A = (X - C λ)^m` (`eq_of_monic_of_associated`).
3. `minpoly.aeval` gives `(A - λ•1)^m = N^m = 0`. If `m < d` then `N^(d-1) = N^m · N^(d-1-m) = 0`, contradicting `shift_pow_pred_ne_zero`. Hence `m = d`.
keyInsights: **One induction powers everything.** The closed-form `shift_pow_apply` — `(N^k) i j = [j = i + k]` — is the only genuinely inductive step in the file. `N^d = 0`, the exact nilpotency index, and (through the minimal-polynomial argument) non-derogatoriness are all corollaries of this single band-shifting picture: each power moves the band of `1`s one diagonal further up-right.

**Multiply on the right to keep the surviving index in range.** Proving the power law via `N^(k+1) = N^k · N` (rather than `N · N^k`) makes the unique nonzero summand sit at column index `j - 1`, which is *always* a valid `Fin d` element whenever it exists (`j ≥ 1`). The mirror choice `N · N^k` would force the index `i + 1`, which can overflow the block and split the argument into extra cases. This is a small but decisive Lean-engineering choice.

**Non-derogatory = minpoly meets its upper and lower bound.** The equality `minpoly = (X - C λ)^d` is a squeeze: the *upper* bound `minpoly ∣ (X-C λ)^d` is pure nilpotency (`N^d = 0`), while the *lower* bound `deg minpoly ≥ d` is pure sharpness (`N^(d-1) ≠ 0`). Primality of `X - C λ` is exactly what converts the divisibility into an exponent comparison, turning two matrix facts into one polynomial identity.

**Sharpness needs a nontrivial ring; nilpotency does not.** `N^d = 0` holds over any commutative ring, but `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` (and hence the exact minimal-polynomial degree) requires `1 ≠ 0`. The file keeps the two hypotheses honestly separated: the nilpotency results are stated over `CommRing R`, the sharpness and minpoly results over `Nontrivial R` / `Field K`.

**Self-containment buys build independence.** Restating `jordanBlock` locally (a three-line `if/else` definition) rather than importing the ~500-line parent means this entry verifies with `import Mathlib` alone, immune to any drift in the parent scaffold — the safer contract for a leaf infrastructure lemma that downstream files will import.

sections.title: §0: Open question, results, and self-containment
sections.summary: Import (`Mathlib` only), top-level docstring stating the sub-OQ-01 position, the list of main results (power law, nilpotency, sharpness, Jordan–Chevalley split, minimal polynomial), and the deliberate self-containment choice; `open Matrix Polynomial` and namespace declaration.
sections.mathContext: Sub-OQ-01 of minpoly-charpoly-oq-01 (Jordan Normal Form infrastructure). Goal: the spectral API of a single Jordan block, needed by the downstream nilpotent-canonical-form and global-assembly sub-questions.

sections.title: §1: The Jordan block and the shift's entrywise form
sections.summary: Defines `jordanBlock R λ d` (λ on the diagonal, 1 on the super-diagonal, 0 elsewhere) and proves `shift_apply`: the nilpotent shift `jordanBlock R 0 d` has entry `(i,j)` equal to 1 exactly on the super-diagonal `j = i + 1`.
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{jordanBlock}\,R\,\lambda\,d = \lambda I + N$ with $N_{ij} = [\,j = i+1\,]$ the strict upper-shift.

sections.title: §2: Power law and nilpotency of the shift
sections.summary: Proves `shift_pow_apply` (the closed form `(N^k) i j = [j = i + k]`, by induction on k with right-multiplication by N), then its immediate corollaries `shift_pow_dim_eq_zero` (`N^d = 0`) and `isNilpotent_shift` (`IsNilpotent N`).
sections.mathContext: $N^k$ has $1$s exactly on the $k$-th super-diagonal ($j = i+k$); at $k=d$ the band leaves the matrix, so $N^d = 0$.

sections.title: §3: Exact nilpotency index
sections.summary: Proves `shift_pow_pred_ne_zero`: over a nontrivial ring and for d ≥ 1, `N^(d-1) ≠ 0` because its (0, d-1) entry is 1. Together with §2 this pins the nilpotency index at exactly d.
sections.mathContext: $N^{d-1}$ has a single surviving $1$ in the top-right corner $(0, d-1)$, so it is nonzero; the nilpotency index of $N$ is exactly $d$.

sections.title: §4: Jordan–Chevalley split of a single block
sections.summary: Proves `jordanBlock_sub_smul_one` (`jordanBlock R λ d - λ • 1 = jordanBlock R 0 d`, i.e. A - λI is the nilpotent shift) and its corollary `sub_smul_one_pow_dim_eq_zero` (`(A - λ • 1)^d = 0`).
sections.mathContext: $A - \lambda I = N$: subtracting the scalar part of a Jordan block leaves the pure nilpotent shift, whose $d$-th power vanishes.

sections.title: §5: Minimal polynomial of a Jordan block
sections.summary: Proves the main theorem `minpoly_jordanBlock`: over a field, `minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d` for d ≥ 1. Upper bound from `(A - λI)^d = 0` + `minpoly.dvd`; exponent pinned by primality of `X - C λ` + `dvd_prime_pow` + monic-associated equality; lower bound forced by `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`.
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{minpoly}_K(\lambda I + N) = (X-\lambda)^d$ — the Jordan block is non-derogatory, its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial.

conclusion.summary: Complete, self-contained discharge of OQ-01-OQ-01: the spectral API of a single Jordan block. A single induction (the power law `(N^k) i j = [j = i + k]`) yields `N^d = 0` and the exact nilpotency index `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`; the Jordan–Chevalley split identifies `A - λI` with the shift; and a UFD squeeze argument delivers the main result `minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d` over a field. Build-verified sorry-free and axiom-free.
conclusion.implications: Supplies the load-bearing single-block facts needed by the downstream sub-questions of minpoly-charpoly-oq-01: the nilpotent canonical form (OQ-01-OQ-02) is built on nilpotent shifts, and the global JNF assembly (OQ-01-OQ-04) needs the minimal/characteristic polynomial of each block. That `minpoly = charpoly` here records that a single Jordan block is non-derogatory (cyclic).
openQuestions: **OQ-01-OQ-02 (nilpotent canonical form)**: extend from a single shift to an arbitrary nilpotent operator — the cyclic-vector / Jordan-basis construction (Axler §8.D). The `shift_pow_apply` band picture and the exact nilpotency index proved here are the model for the general chain-length count.

**Uniqueness of the block sizes**: the invariant that the number of blocks of size ≥ k equals `dim ker N^k − dim ker N^(k-1)` would upgrade the existence results toward a full canonical-form classification; `shift_pow_apply` gives the kernel dimensions of a single block directly.

crossReferences.description: Foundational minpoly | charpoly file and root of the Jordan-Normal-Form strand (the direct parent problem minpoly-charpoly-oq-01 has no standalone gallery entry). This sub-OQ restates `jordanBlock` locally and computes the single-Jordan-block boundary case where minpoly and charpoly coincide (both (X - C λ)^d).

The characteristic polynomial of jordanBlock R λ d is (X - C λ)^d, so Cayley–Hamilton predicts (A - λI)^d = 0; here that annihilation is established directly from the shift's nilpotency and used to bound the minimal polynomial.

mainTheorems.name: shift_pow_apply
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (i j : Fin d), (jordanBlock R 0 d ^ k) i j = if (j : ℕ) = (i : ℕ) + k then (1 : R) else 0
mainTheorems.description: Closed form for the powers of the strict upper-shift N = jordanBlock R 0 d: the k-th power has 1s exactly on the k-th super-diagonal (j = i + k). Proved by induction on k over a general commutative ring, using pow_succ and Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem.
mainTheorems.significance: The single inductive fact from which nilpotency, the exact nilpotency index, and (via the minimal-polynomial argument) non-derogatoriness all follow.

mainTheorems.name: shift_pow_dim_eq_zero
mainTheorems.description: The nilpotent shift raised to the block dimension is zero. Immediate from shift_pow_apply since j < d ≤ i + d makes every entry vanish.
mainTheorems.significance: Nilpotency of the shift (index ≤ d); the upper-bound half of the minimal-polynomial computation.

mainTheorems.name: shift_pow_pred_ne_zero
mainTheorems.description: Over a nontrivial ring the (d-1)-th power of the shift is nonzero, its (0, d-1) entry being 1. With shift_pow_dim_eq_zero this shows the nilpotency index is exactly d.
mainTheorems.significance: Sharpness of the nilpotency index; the lower-bound half of the minimal-polynomial computation.

mainTheorems.name: jordanBlock_sub_smul_one
mainTheorems.statement: jordanBlock R lam d - lam • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) R) = jordanBlock R 0 d
mainTheorems.description: The single-block Jordan–Chevalley split: subtracting the scalar (semisimple) part λI of a Jordan block leaves the pure nilpotent shift.
mainTheorems.significance: Identifies A - λI with the shift, transporting the nilpotency results to a general eigenvalue and feeding the minimal-polynomial argument.

mainTheorems.name: minpoly_jordanBlock
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ (K : Type*) [Field K] (lam : K) (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d → minpoly K (jordanBlock K lam d) = (X - C lam) ^ d
mainTheorems.description: Main result: over a field, the minimal polynomial of a single Jordan block is (X - C λ)^d — equal to its characteristic polynomial. Upper bound from (A - λI)^d = 0 + minpoly.dvd; exponent pinned by primality of X - C λ (dvd_prime_pow + monic-associated equality); lower bound forced by shift_pow_pred_ne_zero.
mainTheorems.significance: Records that a single Jordan block is non-derogatory (cyclic): its minimal and characteristic polynomials coincide. The load-bearing fact for the downstream JNF assembly.
